messages:
alex: Anyone seeing a spike in 502s for edge-model-serving in ap-southeast1? Alerts started ~10m ago and deploys are failing due to image pull/connect timeouts.

deploy-bot: [ALERT] service=edge-model-serving region=ap-southeast1 5xx_rate=18% window=5m

maya: I'm on it. Checking ALB target group health and node logs.

kai: Target group shows most targets UNHEALTHY with health check failures: 502. From ALB logs it looks like we accept connection but backend returns 502. Any recent config changes?

alex: Not that I know of. I tried curl to the health endpoint from a bastion in same subnet: `curl -v https://10.12.5.23:8443/health` -> 200. But the pods themselves are failing to pull artifacts from our object store (timeouts).

maya: Can someone run a tcpdump on a failing node during a pull? I want to see whether SYN/ACKs are returning.

kai: Pasted excerpt from tcpdump on node gpu-node-17 (showing conn to S3 endpoint):
```
12:23:10.123456 IP 10.12.6.17.34567 > s3.internal.amazonaws.com.443: Flags [S], seq 12345, win 64240, options [mss 1460], length 0
12:23:10.124001 IP s3.internal.amazonaws.com.443 > 3.12.6.17.34567: Flags [R], seq 0, ack 0, win 0, length 0
```
That R is suspicious — replies aren't showing SYN/ACK.

alex: I pulled VPC Flow Logs for that time and I see several DENY entries for ephemeral ports range. Example: `Action=DROP protocol=6 srcaddr=3.5.4.6 dstaddr=10.12.6.17 srcport=443 dstport=34567 rule=400 acl-id=nacl-0a1b2c3d`

maya: That matches. There's an NACL applied to the edge subnet that has an explicit DENY for ports 1024-65535 added last week by branch infra-ops (rule name "nacl-block-ephemeral") — I think it was meant to scope inbound, but it ended up denying ephemeral replies.

ops-bot: Created ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OPS-732 — Investigate NACL ephemeral port deny affecting ap-southeast1 edge. Assigned to @maya.

kai: Quick mitigation: I added a allow entry for ephemeral range (1024-65535) for ephemeral outbound replies in the NACL and removed the broad deny. Command used: `aws ec2 replace-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id nacl-0a1b2c3d --rule-number 400 --protocol 6 --port-range From=1024,To=65535 --egress true --rule-action allow --cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0` (run in ops console).

maya: After the change ALB target health started recovering within 45s and image pulls resumed. Confirming rollout is green now. :thumbsup:

alex: Great catch. Did we root-cause why that NACL change was made? Might be human error during a cleanup PR.

maya: Looks like a Terraform PR that attempted to tighten rules for a different subnet, but the module shared the same NACL resource and the change was applied to edge too. I'll add a block to the PR template and add a test to prevent ephemeral block rules on NACLs attached to prod edge subnets.

kai: Postmortem action items I suggest: 1) revert the deny change permanently and add explicit ephemeral allow rules where needed, 2) add an infra-test that simulates outbound connections from nodes to common S3 endpoints, 3) annotate sensitive NACLs so accidental changes require review, 4) run a quick scan across all regions for similar rules.

maya: Filed the follow-ups in OPS-732 and added a short runbook snippet: "If you see image pulls failing but bastion succeeds, check NACL denies for ephemeral port ranges."

alex: Thanks everyone. Marking this resolved for now. We should also notify platform customers who might have been affected. :wave:

deploy-bot: Deployment queue resumed for service=edge-model-serving — 3 pending jobs retried, all succeeded.

kai: Will do a cross-region audit next hour and post results here.

maya: Closing the alert, will attach the terraform diff and remediation steps to the ticket. :white_check_mark:
